Matulionis said the provocations could take various forms, ranging from so-called false flag operations designed to shift blame onto Ukraine to acts of sabotage similar to those seen across Europe in recent years. He said the threat extends beyond the Baltic states to other countries providing strong support for Ukraine. However, he dismissed the possibility of Russia preparing to invade a NATO member state. âThere is certainly no information regarding a troop build-up on our border, so the question of a military invasion is ruled out. The probability here is practically zero,â Matulionis said. Ukraine President Zelensky makes some top military leadership changes and gets into some hot water from his people…. NY Times….. President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine removed his top general on Tuesday night amid swelling public protests and growing concerns that the national unity that had helped the country survive nearly five years of war was in danger of fracturing. The dismissal of the general, Oleksandr Syrskyi, was a major reversal for Mr. Zelensky, who just days earlier sided with him and fired Ukraine’s defense minister , Mykhailo Fedorov. Mr. Zelensky said he was replacing General Syrskyi with Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi, the commander of the Joint Forces. The choice was likely to please the protesters, after Mr. Drapatyi had publicly sided with Mr. Fedorov in his clash with General Syrskyi over warfighting strategy. Thousands of people had joined mass demonstrations to pressure Mr. Zelensky to change course and reaffirm Mr. Fedorov’s vision of warfare as increasingly dominated by drones and robots. As he championed a military overhaul that leaned into high-tech innovation, Mr. Fedorov, 35, emerged as a symbol of hope to many Ukrainians, particularly young people…. … Mr. Zelensky said that he had been forced to choose between Mr. Fedorov and General Syrskyi as the differences between their camps had become impossible to resolve. Ultimately, as the protests grew, it became clear that the rift extended far beyond a clash of personalities. For many Ukrainians, Mr. Fedorov embodied a tech-driven path to victory that might spare lives, while General Syrskyi had come to represent the darkest, most punishing realities of a war fought through sheer attrition…. … After meeting with the president, Mr. Fedorov said a constructive dialogue to address his concerns had begun. “There will definitely be changes,” he said in a statement. Since Ukrainians have largely accepted that there can be no elections while the war rages, mass demonstrations have become a pressure release valve and a check on power…. More… … The Guardian… Medium and long-range strikes against Russia will continue under Mykhailo Drapatyi , Ukraine’s new top military commander, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday, as he replaced Oleksandr Syrskyi in the job after a huge political row accompanied by street protests. “The operations of the Ukrainian defence forces are ​ongoing and must continue steadily,” said the Ukrainian president. “Ukraine’s plan for long-range sanctions and our ‌programme of middle-range strikes will be carried ‌out with absolute precision.” Luke Harding writes that news of Drapatyi’s appointment came in a late-night TV address by Zelenskyy. The president offered a “prominent position” to Mykhailo Fedorov – the defence minister he sacked last week in a shock move that brought out protesters who have given a deadline of Friday for Fedorov to be reinstated. Fedorov welcomed Drapatyi’s appointment as a “breath of fresh air” bringing “new hope to the struggle of free people for freedom and justice”. Zelenskyy paid tribute to Syrskyi , crediting him with leading the defence of Kyiv and launching a counter-invasion of Russia’s Kursk province. Drapatyi, his replacement, is well regarded within Ukraine’s army and liked by the public, Harding writes. He is viewed as an ally of Fedorov , a tech-savvy moderniser. A major general, Drapatyi is commander of Ukraine’s joint forces group and has been fighting Russia since its covert attempt in 2014 to take over the eastern Donbas region. He is famed for driving an infantry fighting vehicle over a barricade set up by pro-Russian militants in Mariupol. The Kremlin lamented the Ukrainian attacks on warehouses of Wildberries – an Amazon-like chain that Kyiv says supplies drone parts and other technologies for the Russian war effort . Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov ​said: “The situation is indeed difficult because of the losses suffered ‌both by the company itself and ‌by representatives of small and medium-sized businesses.” Russian authorities are taking fuel away from Siberia and giving it to Moscow – Russia’s wealthiest and most populous region, where Vladimir Putin most fears losing the support of the Russian elite. The success of Ukrainian drone attacks on oil refineries, storage and shipping has caused fuel crises of varying degrees across Russia. Traders told Reuters that to replace lost production, gasoline produced in the Urals and Siberia, as ⁠well as imported supplies from Belarus, has been redirected to the Moscow region. One of the traders ​said the Achinsk refinery in Siberia’s Krasnoyarsk ​region has been supplying Moscow with fuel. Civilian injuries and deaths increased by more than a third in Ukraine ⁠in the first half of the year, the UN human rights office ⁠said. It documented 1,396 deaths and 7,978 injuries in ⁠the first six months of 2026, representing a 37% increase from the same period last year and a near ⁠doubling versus 2024. Long-range ballistic missiles and drones, and short-range drones and glide bombs drove the escalation. A Russian guided-bomb attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed ⁠at least three ⁠people ​on Tuesday and injured more than a dozen, regional officials said. Two of the dead were ​ in their 60s and the other ‌was 49 . Seven floors of ⁠a nine-storey apartment block were engulfed by flames after the attack, the regional military administration said. ISW. .. Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 21, 2026 Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky dismissed Ukrainian Armed Forces Commander-in-Chief General Oleksandr Syrskyi and appointed the Ukrainian Joint Forces Task Force Commander Major General Mykhailo Drapatyi as his replacement late on July 21. Russian authorities continue costly efforts to mitigate the loss of Russian oil refining capacity due to Ukrainian long-range strikes by subsidizing diesel imports. The Russian government continues exerting legal pressure on Russian migrants likely to coerce migrants into military service under threat of deportation. Polish authorities continue warning of a possible Russian provocation against NATO’s eastern flank. Ukrainian forces struck Russian manufacturing infrastructure and military assets overnight on July 20 and 21. Russia launched 58 drones against Ukraine overnight. Ukrainian forces recently advanced in the Oleksandrivka direction and in northern Kharkiv Oblast. Daily Kos grunt Report for Today….. CÃ©sar JÃ¡uregui Moreno served as attorney general of the northern border state of Chihuahua from 2023 to this year. The involvement of Americans came to light after two US agents said to have worked for the CIA died in a car crash in Chihuahua along with two Mexican law enforcement officers. Attorney General Ernestina Godoy Ramos said JÃ¡uregui had allowed foreign agents to carry out activities reserved for Mexican authorities and had failed to share information. JÃ¡uregui has denied the allegations. The former prosecutor, who is a member of the conservative opposition PAN party, was arrested at the weekend. A court hearing is scheduled for Saturday. A judge must still determine whether there is enough evidence to proceed with the case, Reuters news agency reports. JÃ¡uregui also faces state-level charges in Chihuahua, including of abuse of public office. In a court hearing for those charges on Sunday, he denied that he instructed or consented to the involvement of US agents in the operation. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has come under pressure from US President Donald Trump to crack down on drug trafficking but has repeatedly declined offers of US-led counter-narcotics operations in the country. She has been adamant that foreign officials can only operate on Mexican soil if given prior clearance by the federal government, and has insisted the Latin American nation's sovereignty should not be breached. The crash occurred on 19 April, when a convoy returning from an operation targeting suspected methamphetamine labs in a remote, mountainous area veered off the road and plunged into a ravine. Two members of the Chihuahua State Investigation Agency were killed along with the Americans, officials said. At the time, in his capacity as state attorney general, JÃ¡uregui told a news conference that the Americans had been "instructor officers" from the US embassy engaged in "training work as part of the general and normal exchange we have with the US authorities". US media have reported that the two individuals worked for the CIA as part of an expanded effort to combat narcotics trafficking in the region.
